children: The U.S. plans to release as much as 40 million barrels of oil from its emergency stockpile as the Trump administration seeks to ease fuel prices ahead of the November midterm elections.

The latest release from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve will complete the U.S. contribution of 172 million barrels to an international effort launched after the war with Iran began. The Energy Department also urged European countries to deliver more of the oil they committed to the coordinated action.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said some European members of the International Energy Agency have provided only a portion of their pledged crude and petroleum products. He called on those countries to fulfill their commitments.

Oil and fuel prices have climbed sharply since military operations against Iran began Feb. 28. U.S. gasoline prices remain above $4 a gallon while diesel has risen past $6, adding pressure on the administration as voters prepare for elections that will determine control of Congress.

The latest drawdown is expected to leave the SPR at its lowest level since 1982, limiting the government's ability to make further non-emergency releases. Wright has indicated another drawdown is unlikely. Federal law restricts non-emergency releases once the reserve falls below 252.4 million barrels.

The oil is being provided through exchanges rather than outright sales. Companies will repay the government with additional barrels, which the Energy Department expects will return about 200 million barrels to the reserve over the next year. Bids for the latest release are due Oct. 6 at 11 a.m. Central time.

title: U.S. to release 40M more barrels from oil reserve as fuel prices surge
